guides.title: Change a heading
guides.summary: Edit the words at the top of a section, then publish.
guides.body:
Headings are the large titles on your pages. You can change any of them in a minute.

## Steps

1. Open **Edit your website** from Start here.
2. Click the heading you want to change. It becomes editable.
3. Type the new words. Keep it short: about **8 words** reads best.
4. Click **Publish** when you are happy.

## Good to know

- Each page has **one main heading** at the very top. Other headings in the page are section titles.
- Changes stay as a **draft** until you publish, so nobody sees half-finished work.
- Prefer a form? Open the page in **Pages**, find the section and edit its **Title** field.

guides.title: Replace a photo
guides.summary: Swap a picture and keep it sharp and accessible.
guides.body:
A new photo takes the same place as the old one, so the layout stays tidy.

## Steps

1. Open the page, then open the section that holds the photo.
2. Click the photo, then **Remove** (or drag the new file onto it).
3. Upload your new photo from your computer.
4. Drag the small circle (the **hotspot**) onto the most important part, such as a face. The photo then crops around it.
5. Fill in the **Alternative text** field. See below.
6. Click **Publish**.

## Choosing a good photo

- Each photo field shows a **Recommended** size. Aim for that size or larger.
- Use the right shape for the spot (landscape, portrait or square).
- Avoid photos with words in them. Screen readers cannot read the words.

## Alternative text

Describe what the photo shows in one short sentence, for example "Two electricians fitting a switchboard". It helps people using screen readers and it helps Google. Leave it empty only if the photo is purely decoration.

guides.title: Publish and undo
guides.summary: Make changes live, or step back to an earlier version.
guides.body:
Nothing you edit goes live until you publish it.

## Publish

1. Make your changes. They save automatically as a **draft**.
2. Read them over. Use **Edit your website** to see the page as visitors will.
3. Click **Publish**. Your site updates within a minute.

## Undo a mistake

- **Not published yet?** Open the menu next to **Publish** and choose **Discard changes**. The page goes back to the live version.
- **Already published?** Open the menu next to **Publish** and choose **Review changes** or **History**. Pick an earlier version and click **Restore**, then publish again.

## Take something off the site

Open the menu next to **Publish** and choose **Unpublish**. The page disappears from the site but stays in the Studio, so you can bring it back later.

## Good to know

- Every version is kept, so you can always go back.
- If two people edit at once, you will see each other's changes appear.

guides.title: Write a blog post
guides.summary: Start a new article, add a picture and publish it.
guides.body:
## Steps

1. From Start here, click **Write a blog post**.
2. Add a **Title**. Keep it under about **60 characters** so it fits in search results.
3. Check the **Slug**. This is the page address. Short and plain is best.
4. Write a **short summary** of one or two sentences. It appears on the blog list and in search results.
5. Add a **main image** and its alternative text. See "Replace a photo".
6. Write the article in the body. Use headings to break up long text and keep paragraphs short.
7. Choose a **category** and an **author**.
8. Click **Publish**.

## Good to know

- Set a **publish date** to keep the order of posts right.
- A post stays a draft until you publish, so you can come back to it later.

guides.title: Update opening hours
guides.summary: Change your hours, holiday closures and contact details.
guides.body:
Your opening hours, phone number and address live in one place. Change them once and they update everywhere they appear, such as the footer.

## Steps

1. From Start here, click **Business info and opening hours**.
2. Find **Opening hours**. Each row covers a set of days with the same hours, for example Monday to Friday.
3. Change the **Opens** and **Closes** times. Use 24-hour time, such as 08:00 or 17:30.
4. Tick **Closed on these days** for days you do not open. Days without a row show as closed.
5. Check the phone number and address while you are there.
6. Click **Publish**.

## Public holidays and special days

Use **Public holidays and special days** for one-off changes, such as Christmas Day. Days that have passed disappear from the site by themselves, so there is nothing to tidy up afterwards.

## Good to know

- Two rows for the same day make a split shift, such as a lunch break.
- The site and Google both read these hours, so keep them accurate.

guides.title: Add a team member
guides.summary: Add a person to the team section, with a photo.
guides.body:
## Steps

1. Open **Team** in the left-hand menu, then click **Create new**.
2. Fill in their **name** and **role**.
3. Upload their **portrait** and fill in its alternative text. Use the same shape for everyone so the cards line up. See "Replace a photo".
4. Add a **short bio**. Two or three sentences is plenty.
5. Click **Publish**.

## Change the order

Drag people up or down in the Team list. The site follows the same order.

## Remove someone

Open their entry, open the menu next to **Publish** and choose **Unpublish** to hide them, or **Delete** to remove them for good.

guides.title: Change your logo or browser icon
guides.summary: Update the logo, site name and the small picture in browser tabs.
guides.body:
The logo and site name show in the header. The browser icon is the small picture in browser tabs and bookmarks.

## Steps

1. In the sidebar, open **Website settings**, then **Name, logo & icon**.
2. To change the logo, upload a new one in the **Logo** field. An SVG or a transparent PNG works best.
3. To change the browser icon, find **Browser icon**. Choose **Upload an icon** and add a square picture, or choose **Use the site logo** and crop it square.
4. Check the preview below the icon. At the smallest size, a plain mark reads better than small text.
5. Click **Publish**.

## Good to know

- The browser icon works best as a square PNG or SVG, at least 512 px wide.
- Browsers keep old icons for a while. If you still see the old one, close the tab and reopen the site.
- The site name and description on this screen are also what search engines show.
